title: JSON Schema Drift Detector for Model & Config Rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Implement an automated detector that identifies quality regressions for structured (JSON) outputs tied to model or configuration changes (model version, quantization, decoding params, prompt templates, reranking).
Background: We have ad-hoc schema checks in the eval harness but regressions slip through when configs change (e.g., new temperature/beam settings) or when we onboard quantized model variants. This ticket scopes a production-ready pipeline that (1) computes JSON schema adherence metrics per-request and per-release, (2) surfaces trends in the Console, and (3) gates rollouts via CI/canaries and alerts on significant degradation.
Proposed solution: 1) Define a canonical "schema-adherence" metric set: parse_success_rate, missing_field_rate, extraneous_field_rate, type_mismatch_rate, and normalized_schema_score (0-100). Each metric is calculated per-test-case and aggregated over windows (1h, 24h, 7d) and by cohort (model, config, route, region, customer tier). 2) Build an ingestion hook in the evals pipeline that emits per-response schema metrics to our telemetry stream (metrics + traces). 3) Implement drift detection rules: - Absolute drop: normalized_schema_score drop >= 7 points vs baseline OR - Relative error rate spike: parse_failure_rate increase >= 150% vs historical median OR - New-field regression: missing_field_rate increase >= 10% for any required field
4) Integrate alerts: - Paging for P0 regressions (score drop >= 12 points or >50% parse failures) - Slack/email for P1/P2 warnings - Console dashboard with per-field heatmap and ranked failing examples
5) CI & rollout gating: - Add a lightweight CI job that runs the golden prompt set against proposed model/config changes and fails the PR if schema_score drop > 5 points. - Canary rollout integration: run golden set on canary traffic and auto-block majority rollout if alert triggers.
6) Reduce false positives: - Allow per-route expected schema variants (schema overrides) and configurable thresholds. - Maintain a short-term whitelist of known noisy prompts during model transfers.
Instrumentation details: - Use existing eval harness (eval-service) to run the golden set and emit structured metrics to metrics-store (histograms for scores). - Store top-k failing responses in object store with links in the console. - Tag metrics with model_id, model_tag, quantization_profile, decode_params, route, customer_id (if present) and commit sha for reproducibility. - Provide a small UI panel in Console -> Rollouts showing schema_score delta and example failures.
Rollout plan: - Week 1 (spike): prototype metric computation and run on past 90 days of stored evals to compute baselines. - Week 2: emit metrics from eval-service for new runs and wire up dashboard. - Week 3: CI job + small canary integration + alert rules. - Week 4: tune thresholds and onboard two internal product routes (chat and form-parsing).
Risks and mitigations: - Noise from non-deterministic outputs: mitigate by focusing on required fields and using relaxed type checks for known unstable fields. - Storage cost of example captures: retain only 1000 most recent failing examples per model/config. - Performance: evaluation CI job must finish within acceptable PR time — use golden set subset for CI (20-50 examples) and full set for nightly runs.
acceptance_criteria: A metrics pipeline exists that emits per-response JSON schema metrics (parse_success_rate, missing_field_rate, extraneous_field_rate, type_mismatch_rate, normalized_schema_score).
A Console dashboard shows schema_score by model/config/route with drilldown to top failing examples and per-field heatmap.
Alerting rules are created for absolute and relative regression conditions and wired to Slack + paging for P0.
A CI check runs the golden prompt subset on PRs that change model/config and blocks merges when schema_score drops > 5 points.
Canary rollout integration blocks majority rollouts when configured alert conditions are met.
False-positive controls: per-route schema overrides and a documented tuning guide are available.
Runbook created for investigating schema regressions with example triage steps and links to captured artifacts.
